To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the catalytic mechanism of S ribosylhomocys-teinase involves an Fe2+ ion and a series of keto intermediates.
the mechanism of S-ribo-sylhomocysteiinase (LuxS), the enzyme that produces the bacterial quorum sensing molecule AI-2, involves a novel redox reaction that shifts the carbonyl oxygen from C1 to C3.

the catalytic mechanism of S-Ribosulpho-homocysteinase involves the formation of a 2-keto- and 3-hydroxy-ribosyl intermediate and that the active site contains a general acid/base residue that is required for proton transfer during the reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the catalytic mechanism of S ribosylhomocystsine (SRH).
understanding the catalytic mechanism of the S-ribosylation reaction.
understanding the molecular basis for the catalytic mechanism of S-Ribosylation, a ubiquitous reaction in nature, which is catalyzed by the enzyme S-Ribosyllhomocysteinases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the catalytic mechanism of S-RH cleavage is similar to that proposed for the cleavage of S-adenosylmethionine by AdoMet decarboxylase, except that the carbonyl oxygen is transferred to the C-2 position of the substrate in AdoMet decaboxylase and the C-3 in S-RH cleaving enzyme LuxS.
the mechanism of SRH hydrolysis is a concerted process involving a metal-assisted redox reaction and a beta-elimination reaction.
the mechanism of LuxS catalysis is an example of a new type of thioether cleavage reaction that is initiated by an internal redox mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LuxS is the first metalloenzyme that catalyzes the beta-elimination of a thioether bond and that this enzyme contains a unique mechanism for the cleavage of thioether linkages.
the catalytic mechanism of the LuxS enzyme involves an internal redox process in which the Fe2+ ion is the catalyst for the shift in the carbonyl from C-1 to C-3.
we have demonstrated the presence of keto intermediates in the LuxS catalytic reaction, and we have demonstrated the chemical competence of the 2-keto compound.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism of LuxS is a new type of reaction that is not found in the current enzyme classification.
we identified the intermediates in the mechanism for the LuxS enzyme, which is a key enzyme in the AI-2 quorum sensing system.
the mechanism for the cleavage of SRH by LuxS involves an unusual internal redox reaction that results in the transfer of a carbonyl group.
